Command: Escape Sodom, Do Not Look Back
Summary: The angels' command to Lot as Sodom's judgment fell: escape for your life, do not look behind, do not stay in the plain, escape to the mountain.
Commandment: Escape for thy life; look not behind thee, neither stay thou in all the plain; escape to the mountain.
Application: One moment, one household, one road out. Lot's wife looked back and became a pillar of salt (Genesis 19:26) — the warning inside the command, fulfilled in the same chapter. Lot's plea for Zoar (Genesis 19:20) does not change the command's form.
Purpose: To rescue Lot's household alive from a judgment already falling, with no delay and no backward glance (Genesis 19:17).
Function: One moment, one household, one road out. Given once, for one moment — a one-time command, so the threefold division does not apply to it. Its goal was to rescue Lot's household alive from a judgment already falling, with no delay and no backward glance. The evil it addressed was the judgment itself — and the backward look that would share in it. It restrained that evil by the escape itself: escape for your life, do not look behind, do not stay in the plain. Lot's wife looked back, and became a pillar of salt.
